en.v: The short ribs can be braised a day in advance; refrigerate them whole in their cooking liquid. The finished short rib curry can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on stovetop before serving.

en.t: 900 g boneless beef short ribs,
Kosher salt
3 tbsp (45 ml) vegetable oil, divided
240 ml full-fat coconut milk, such as Aroy-D, divided
115 g homemade or store-bought massaman curry paste
3 tbsp (75 g) palm sugar
3 tbsp (80 g) tamarind paste
3 tbsp (45 ml) fish sauce
325 g Yukon gold potatoes (2 medium potatoes), cut into 6.5 cm pieces
Cooked jasmine rice, for serving

1. For the Beef Braise: Season beef all over with salt. In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, heat half of the oil over medium-high heat until lightly smoking. Add half of the beef and cook, turning occasionally, until browned on all sides, 5 to 6 minutes; transfer browned short ribs to a plate. Add remaining oil to the pot and repeat the browning process with the rest of the beef. Allow beef to cool for 5 minutes, then cut into roughly 5 × 6.5 cm pieces.

2. Return all beef and any accumulated juices to the pot and add enough water to fully cover (about 2000–3000 ml). Bring to a vigorous simmer, partially cover, and cook, stirring occasionally and adding more water as needed to keep beef submerged, until beef is fully tender and can be pierced easily with a paring knife, 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours. Remove pot from heat and set aside to cool, keeping beef submerged in cooking liquid, for at least 30 minutes. When cool, transfer beef to a plate, and set aside along with 475 ml of beef cooking liquid and 3 tbsp (45 ml) rendered beef fat, which should have risen to the surface of cooking liquid; remaining cooking liquid and fat can be refrigerated or frozen in an airtight container and saved for another use.

3. For the Curry: In a saucepan, combine reserved rendered beef fat and 120 ml coconut milk and bring to a simmer over medium-low heat. Cook, stirring often with a rubber spatula, until thickened slightly, about 3 minutes.

4. Add curry paste, and use a rubber spatula to vigorously stir and work paste into coconut milk mixture until thoroughly combined, 2 to 3 minutes. (This requires a good amount of effort, as the paste is so stiff.) Cook, stirring and scraping constantly while gradually adding remaining 120 ml coconut milk in 2-tbsp (30 ml) increments, until paste turns dark red and the fat begins to separate from curry paste, about 10 minutes.

5. Add palm sugar, tamarind, and fish sauce, and stir to melt palm sugar. Add potatoes and stir to evenly coat with curry mixture. Add beef and reserved beef cooking liquid and bring to a simmer. Continue to cook, adjusting heat as needed to maintain a steady simmer, until potatoes are tender and a knife meets little resistance when inserted into a piece of potato, and curry is reduced to a thick, saucy consistency with a layer of separated fat on the surface, about 30 minutes. Remove from heat.
6. Transfer curry to a large serving bowl or divide between individual bowls. Serve with cooked jasmine rice.

1. Dusené hovädzie: mäso zo všetkých strán osolíme. Vo veľkom hrnci s hrubým dnom alebo liatinovom hrnci rozohrejeme na stredne silnom ohni polovicu oleja, kým nezačne jemne dymiť. Vložíme polovicu mäsa a za občasného obracania ho opekáme, kým nie je zo všetkých strán zhnednuté, 5 až 6 minút; opečené rebrá preložíme na tanier. Do hrnca pridáme zvyšný olej a rovnako opečieme zvyšok mäsa. Mäso necháme 5 minút chladnúť, potom ho nakrájame na kusy približne 5 × 6,5 cm.

2. Všetko mäso aj s nazbieranou šťavou vrátime do hrnca a zalejeme toľkou vodou, aby bolo úplne ponorené (asi 2000 – 3000 ml). Privedieme do silného varu, čiastočne prikryjeme a varíme za občasného miešania, podľa potreby dolievame vodu, aby mäso zostalo ponorené, kým nie je úplne mäkké a ľahko ho prepichneme nožíkom, 1 hodinu 45 minút až 2 hodiny. Hrniec odstavíme a necháme chladnúť aspoň 30 minút; mäso pritom necháme ponorené vo výpare. Vychladnuté mäso preložíme na tanier a odložíme spolu so 475 ml výparu a 3 PL (45 ml) vyškvareného hovädzieho tuku, ktorý by mal vyplávať na povrch; zvyšný výpar a tuk môžeme vo vzduchotesnej nádobe uložiť do chladničky alebo zamraziť a použiť inokedy.

3. Kari: v hrnci zmiešame odložený hovädzí tuk a 120 ml kokosového mlieka a na stredne slabom ohni privedieme do mierneho varu. Za častého miešania gumenou stierkou varíme, kým trochu nezhustne, asi 3 minúty.

4. Pridáme kari pastu a gumenou stierkou ju energicky miešame a vpracúvame do kokosovej zmesi, kým sa dôkladne nespojí, 2 až 3 minúty. (Vyžaduje si to dosť námahy, pasta je veľmi tuhá.) Za stáleho miešania a zoškrabovania pridávame postupne po 2 PL (30 ml) zvyšných 120 ml kokosového mlieka a varíme, kým pasta nie je tmavočervená a tuk sa od nej nezačne oddeľovať, asi 10 minút.

5. Pridáme palmový cukor, tamarind a rybaciu omáčku a miešame, kým sa palmový cukor neroztopí. Pridáme zemiaky a premiešame, aby sa rovnomerne obalili kari zmesou. Pridáme mäso a odložený výpar a privedieme do mierneho varu. Varíme ďalej, podľa potreby regulujeme oheň, aby sa kari stále mierne varilo, kým zemiaky nezmäknú a nôž do nich vojde takmer bez odporu a kari sa nezredukuje na hustú omáčku s vrstvou oddeleného tuku na povrchu, asi 30 minút. Odstavíme.
6. Kari preložíme do veľkej servírovacej misy alebo rozdelíme do misiek. Podávame s uvarenou jazmínovou ryžou.

en.t: 355 ml full-fat coconut milk, such as Aroy-D, divided
10 fresh or frozen makrut lime leaves, divided
2 tbsp (30 ml) virgin coconut oil
115 g homemade or store-bought green curry paste
1 tbsp plus 2 tsp (35 g) palm sugar
3 tbsp (45 ml) fish sauce
450 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 5 cm pieces
Kosher salt
5 Thai eggplants (about 150 g total), stemmed, quartered, and placed in a small bowl of water
30 g fresh sweet basil leaves (a.k.a. Thai basil)
Cooked jasmine rice, for serving

1. In a small bowl, whisk together 120 ml coconut milk and 120 ml water; set thinned coconut milk mixture aside. Remove and discard the mid-rib from the makrut lime leaves; set 8 of the leaves aside. Stack remaining 2 makrut lime leaves, fold in half widthwise, then slice into hair-thin strips; set aside separately.
2. In a saucepan, combine coconut oil with 120 ml coconut milk and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook, stirring often with a rubber spatula, until thickened slightly, about 1 minute.

3. Add curry paste, stir vigorously to combine, and use a rubber spatula to scrape sides of the saucepan to fully incorporate paste. Raise heat to medium-high and cook, stirring and scraping constantly until paste mixture begins to spit (which indicates that water content has been cooked off, and mixture has begun to fry in coconut oil), about 1 minute. Lower heat back to medium, and continue to cook while gradually adding remaining 120 ml coconut milk in 2-tbsp (30 ml) increments, until paste darkens slightly and the fat begins to separate from curry paste, 5 to 6 minutes.

4. Add fish sauce and palm sugar, and stir until palm sugar is fully dissolved, about 30 seconds. Lightly season chicken on all sides with salt, add to saucepan with reserved whole makrut lime leaves, and stir to evenly coat with curry paste mixture. Add reserved thinned coconut milk mixture and bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, until chicken is cooked through and tender and liquid has thickened slightly, about 10 minutes.

5. Add eggplants, and continue to cook, adjusting heat as needed to maintain a simmer, until eggplants are just cooked through but still have some bite to them, about 3 minutes. Remove from heat, add sweet basil, and stir until wilted and incorporated.
6. Transfer curry to a large serving bowl or divide between individual bowls, and garnish with reserved thinly-sliced makrut lime leaves. Serve with cooked jasmine rice.

1. V malej miske metličkou zmiešame 120 ml kokosového mlieka so 120 ml vody; zriedené kokosové mlieko odložíme. Z listov kafírovej limetky odstránime a vyhodíme strednú žilku; 8 listov odložíme. Zvyšné 2 listy položíme na seba, priečne preložíme na polovicu a nakrájame na tenučké prúžky; odložíme zvlášť.
2. V hrnci zmiešame kokosový olej so 120 ml kokosového mlieka a na strednom ohni privedieme do mierneho varu. Za častého miešania gumenou stierkou varíme, kým trochu nezhustne, asi 1 minútu.

3. Pridáme kari pastu, energicky premiešame a gumenou stierkou zoškrabujeme steny hrnca, aby sa pasta úplne zapracovala. Oheň zvýšime na stredne silný a za stáleho miešania a zoškrabovania varíme, kým pasta nezačne prskať (znamená to, že sa voda odparila a zmes sa začala opekať v kokosovom oleji), asi 1 minútu. Oheň stiahneme späť na stredný a varíme ďalej, pričom postupne po 2 PL (30 ml) pridávame zvyšných 120 ml kokosového mlieka, kým pasta trochu nestmavne a tuk sa od nej nezačne oddeľovať, 5 až 6 minút.

4. Pridáme rybaciu omáčku a palmový cukor a miešame, kým sa cukor úplne nerozpustí, asi 30 sekúnd. Kuracie mäso zo všetkých strán zľahka osolíme, pridáme do hrnca spolu s odloženými celými listami kafírovej limetky a premiešame, aby sa rovnomerne obalilo kari pastou. Prilejeme odložené zriedené kokosové mlieko a privedieme do mierneho varu. Za občasného miešania varíme, kým mäso nie je hotové a mäkké a tekutina trochu nezhustne, asi 10 minút.

5. Pridáme baklažány a varíme ďalej, podľa potreby regulujeme oheň, aby sa kari mierne varilo, kým baklažány nie sú práve uvarené, no stále na skus, asi 3 minúty. Odstavíme, pridáme sladkú bazalku a miešame, kým nezvädne a nezapracuje sa.
6. Kari preložíme do veľkej servírovacej misy alebo rozdelíme do misiek a ozdobíme odloženými prúžkami listov kafírovej limetky. Podávame s uvarenou jazmínovou ryžou.

en.v: Rendang can be made over several days. The spice paste can be made up to 2 days ahead and stored in a tightly sealed container in the refrigerator. The rendang can be prepared through step 4 up to 3 days in advance; cool it to room temperature and transfer it to the refrigerator. To continue cooking, proceed with step 5 of the recipe. Rendang can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to one week and frozen for up to 6 months.

sk.v: Rendang môžeme pripravovať aj niekoľko dní. Korenistú pastu môžeme pripraviť až 2 dni vopred a uchovávať v dobre uzavretej nádobe v chladničke. Rendang môžeme pripraviť po krok 4 až 3 dni vopred; necháme ho vychladnúť na izbovú teplotu a preložíme do chladničky. Pri pokračovaní nadviažeme krokom 5 receptu. Rendang môžeme uchovávať v uzatvárateľnej nádobe v chladničke až týždeň a zmraziť až na 6 mesiacov.

c.t: Asian shallots are about 4 cm long, much smaller than regular shallots; they are sold in Asian grocery stores.
Candlenuts (kemiri) are mildly toxic raw and are used as a thickener; macadamias are a good substitute.

You can add 150 g baby potatoes (scrubbed, halved if large) with the beef. Makrut lime leaves, lemongrass, galangal and wet tamarind are sold in Asian markets; 2 to 3 daun salam and/or turmeric leaves make it even more aromatic.
Ázijské šalotky sú dlhé asi 4 cm, oveľa menšie ako bežné; dostanete ich v ázijských obchodoch.
Kemiri (orechy tung/candlenut) sú surové mierne jedovaté a používajú sa na zahustenie; dobrou náhradou sú makadamové orechy.

S mäsom môžete pridať 150 g malých zemiakov (vydrhnutých, väčšie prekrojených). Listy kafírovej limetky, citrónovú trávu, galangal a tamarindovú dreň dostanete v ázijských obchodoch; 2 až 3 listy daun salam a/alebo kurkumy jedlo ešte prevoňajú.

en.t: 1. Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat to 160 °C (fan 140 °C).

2. For the Spice Paste: In the bowl of a food processor, pulse shallots, chiles, galangal, ginger, garlic, candlenuts, coriander seeds, turmeric, and salt, stopping and scraping down sides as needed, until thick paste forms, 2 to 3 minutes. (Spice paste should have the texture of cooked oatmeal; use a rubber spatula to scrape the sides of the bowl as needed. If the paste isn’t coming together, add water 1 tbsp (15 ml) at a time.)

3. For the Rendang: In a 4730 ml or 5680 ml Dutch oven, combine spice paste, coconut milk, makrut lime leaves, lemongrass, cinnamon stick, and tamarind. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce heat to low and add beef, stirring to evenly coat with sauce. (Don’t worry if beef isn’t completely submerged.)

4. Transfer to oven and cook, uncovered, until sauce is reduced and a puddle of oil appears on the surface, about 2 hours, stirring every 30 minutes. At this point, the dish is ready to eat; you can stop cooking here or, for a more traditional rendang, proceed with the remaining steps.

5. Wearing oven mitts, carefully transfer pot to stovetop and bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat. Using a flexible, heat-proof spatula, stir and scrape the bottom and sides frequently, and cook, uncovered, until the meat is tender, the sauce has reduced and darkened, and any remaining sauce is clinging to the beef, 45 minutes to 1 hour. Serve immediately with white rice and sambal, if desired.

sk.t: 1. Mriežku v rúre dáme do strednej polohy a rúru predhrejeme na 160 °C (teplovzdušnú na 140 °C).

2. Korenistá pasta: v nádobe kuchynského robota pulzne mixujeme šalotky, čili papričky, galangal, zázvor, cesnak, kukui orechy, koriander, kurkumu a soľ, podľa potreby prestaneme a zoškrabeme steny, kým nevznikne hustá pasta, 2 až 3 minúty. (Pasta má mať konzistenciu uvarenej ovsenej kaše; steny nádoby podľa potreby zoškrabujeme gumenou stierkou. Ak sa pasta nespája, pridávame vodu po 1 PL (15 ml).)

3. Rendang: v liatinovom hrnci s objemom 4730 ml alebo 5680 ml zmiešame korenistú pastu, kokosové mlieko, listy kafírovej limetky, citrónovú trávu, škoricu a tamarind. Na strednom ohni privedieme do mierneho varu. Oheň stiahneme na minimum, pridáme mäso a premiešame, aby sa rovnomerne obalilo omáčkou. (Nevadí, ak mäso nie je úplne ponorené.)

4. Hrniec vložíme do rúry a bez pokrievky pečieme, kým sa omáčka nezredukuje a na povrchu sa neobjaví mláka oleja, asi 2 hodiny; každých 30 minút premiešame. V tejto fáze je jedlo hotové; môžeme tu skončiť, alebo pre tradičnejší rendang pokračujeme ďalšími krokmi.

5. V chňapkách hrniec opatrne preložíme na sporák a na stredne slabom ohni privedieme do mierneho varu. Pružnou žiaruvzdornou stierkou často miešame a zoškrabujeme dno a steny a bez pokrievky varíme, kým mäso nie je mäkké, omáčka sa nezredukuje a nestmavne a jej zvyšok nepriľne k mäsu, 45 minút až 1 hodinu. Ihneď podávame s bielou ryžou, prípadne so sambalom.

175 ml hot water, plus 175 ml tap water

2 onions, chopped fine
1½ tsp (9 g) table salt, divided
1 tomato, cored and chopped coarse
4 (170–225 g) boneless, skinless chicken breasts, trimmed and cut into 4 cm pieces
3 whole cloves
2 cinnamon sticks
2 bay leaves
4 garlic cloves, minced to paste
1 tsp (5 ml) grated fresh ginger
1 tsp (5 ml) ground coriander
1 tsp (5 ml) ground turmeric
½ tsp (2.5 ml) pepper
¼ tsp (1.2 ml) ground cardamom
¼ tsp (1.2 ml) cayenne pepper
235 ml coarsely chopped cilantro leaves and tender stems
Plain yogurt

1. Process 3 tbsp (44 ml) roasted cashews in blender on low speed to consistency of fine gravel mixed with sand, 10 to 15 seconds. Add 175 ml hot water and process on low speed until combined, about 5 seconds. Scrape down sides of blender jar and let mixture sit for 15 minutes.

2. Meanwhile, heat 3 tbsp (44 ml) extra-virgin olive oil in Dutch oven over medium heat until shimmering. Add 2 finely chopped onions and ¼ tsp (1.2 ml) table salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until dark golden brown, adjusting heat as needed if beginning to scorch, 10 to 15 minutes.

3. Transfer onions to blender jar along with 1 cored and coarsely chopped tomato and process on low speed until coarse puree forms, about 1 minute. Scrape down sides of blender jar, then process on high speed until sauce is completely smooth, about 1 minute.

4. Pat dry 4 chicken breasts, trimmed and cut into 4 cm pieces, with paper towels and sprinkle with 1 tsp (5 ml) salt. Heat remaining 2 tbsp (30 ml) oil in now-empty pot over medium heat until shimmering. Add 3 whole cloves, 2 cinnamon sticks, and 2 bay leaves and cook, stirring occasionally, until fragrant, 30 to 60 seconds. Add 4 garlic cloves, minced to paste; 1 tsp (5 ml) grated ginger; 1 tsp (5 ml) ground coriander; 1 tsp (5 ml) ground turmeric; ½ tsp (2.5 ml) pepper; ¼ tsp (1.2 ml) ground cardamom; and ¼ tsp (1.2 ml) cayenne pepper and cook until fragrant, 30 to 60 seconds. Add cashew-onion mixture, 175 ml tap water, and remaining ¼ tsp (1.2 ml) salt and stir, scraping up any brown bits from bottom of pot. Bring to simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer gently for 10 minutes.

5. Stir in chicken, increase heat to medium, and return to simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer gently until chicken registers 70 °C, 10 to 15 minutes. Discard bay leaves and cinnamon. Sprinkle korma with 235 ml coarsely chopped cilantro leaves and tender stems and 2 tbsp (30 ml) chopped cashews and serve with plain yogurt.

en.t: 1 small bunch cilantro stems, leaves and thin stems reserved for another use

4 whole cloves garlic

2 thin slices fresh ginger
1 stalk lemongrass, bottom 10 cm only, roughly chopped
1 whole dried Thai bird chile (or 1 whole chile de arbol), more or less to taste
1 tsp (5 ml) makrut lime zest, or 2 whole makrut lime leaves
1 tsp (5 ml) whole coriander seed
6 pods Thai black cardamom or 1 pod green cardamom, inner seeds only
Kosher salt

235 ml vegetable or canola oil

2 (425 g) cans coconut milk, or 475 ml fresh coconut milk (do not shake)

4 chicken legs, split into drumsticks and thighs
Fish sauce, to taste
Sliced shallots, lime wedges, and pickled Chinese mustard greens, for serving

1. Place cilantro stems, shallots, garlic, turmeric, ginger, lemongrass, chile, lime zest, coriander seed, and cardamom in the center of a 30 × 30 cm square of heavy-duty aluminum foil. Gather up edges to make a tight pouch. Place pouch directly over the flame of a gas burner and cook, turning occasionally, until aromatic and wisps of smoke begin to rise, about 8 minutes. If no gas burner is available, place the pouch in the bottom of a wok or cast iron skillet and heat over high heat, turning occasionally, until smoky, about 10 minutes. Allow contents to cool slightly and transfer to a large mortar and pestle.
2. Add a large pinch of salt to the aromatics. Pound until a very fine paste is formed, about 10 minutes. Add shrimp paste and pound to incorporate. Set curry paste mixture aside.

3. Separate out 1/4 of the noodles (enough noodles to make a crispy fried-noodle topping for 4 bowls) and set the remaining noodles aside. Heat vegetable oil in a large wok over high heat until shimmering. Working in batches, add noodles to oil and fry, stirring and flipping until golden brown and crisp. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate. Season with salt and set aside.

4. Discard all but 1 tbsp (15 ml) oil from wok. Using a spoon, skim 2 tbsp (30 ml) of creamy fat off the top of the coconut milk and add to the wok. Heat wok over high heat and cook, stirring constantly, until coconut milk breaks and oil begins to lightly smoke, about 2 minutes. Add curry paste mixture and cook, stirring and smearing the paste into the oil, until aromatic, about 45 seconds.

5. Slowly stir in the coconut milk, followed by the chicken stock and palm sugar. Add chicken legs and bring to a simmer. Cook, turning chicken occasionally, until chicken is tender and broth is very flavorful, about 30 minutes. Season to taste with fish sauce.

6. Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add remaining uncooked noodles and cook until al dente, about 1 minute. Drain noodles and divide between four warmed bowls. Top noodles with two pieces of chicken. Divide broth evenly between bowls. Top with fried noodles and serve immediately with sliced shallots, lime wedges, and pickled mustard greens on the side.

Okraje zdvihneme a vytvoríme tesne uzavretý balíček. Balíček položíme priamo nad plameň plynového horáka a za občasného obracania opekáme, kým nezavonia a nezačnú z neho stúpať prúžky dymu, asi 8 minút. Ak nemáme plynový sporák, balíček položíme na dno woku alebo liatinovej panvice a na veľkom ohni ho za občasného obracania zohrievame, kým nezačne voňať dymom, asi 10 minút. Obsah necháme trochu vychladnúť a preložíme do veľkého mažiara.
2. K aromatickým surovinám pridáme veľkú štipku soli. Roztĺkame, kým nevznikne veľmi jemná pasta, asi 10 minút. Pridáme krevetovú pastu a roztĺkame, kým sa nezapracuje. Kari pastu odložíme.

3. Oddelíme ¼ rezancov (toľko, aby sme mali chrumkavé vysmážané rezance navrch do 4 misiek) a zvyšné rezance odložíme. Vo veľkom woku rozohrejeme na veľkom ohni rastlinný olej, kým sa nezačne vlniť. Po dávkach do oleja vkladáme rezance a za miešania a obracania ich vyprážame, kým nie sú zlatohnedé a chrumkavé. Preložíme na tanier vyložený papierovou utierkou. Osolíme a odložíme.

4. Z woku vylejeme všetok olej okrem 1 PL (15 ml). Lyžicou zoberieme z povrchu kokosového mlieka 2 PL (30 ml) hustej smotanovej vrstvy a dáme ju do woku. Wok zohrejeme na veľkom ohni a za stáleho miešania varíme, kým sa kokosové mlieko nerozdelí a olej nezačne jemne dymiť, asi 2 minúty. Pridáme kari pastu a za stáleho miešania a rozotierania pasty v oleji ju opekáme, kým nezavonia, asi 45 sekúnd.

5. Pomaly vmiešame kokosové mlieko, potom kurací vývar a palmový cukor. Pridáme kuracie stehná a privedieme do mierneho varu. Za občasného obracania mäsa varíme, kým mäso nie je mäkké a vývar veľmi chutný, asi 30 minút. Podľa chuti dochutíme rybacou omáčkou.

6. V hrnci privedieme do varu osolenú vodu. Pridáme zvyšné surové rezance a uvaríme ich al dente, asi 1 minútu. Rezance scedíme a rozdelíme do štyroch nahriatych misiek. Na rezance položíme po dva kúsky mäsa. Vývar rovnomerne rozdelíme do misiek. Navrch dáme vysmážané rezance a ihneď podávame s nakrájanými šalotkami, mesiačikmi limetky a nakladanou horčicovou zeleninou bokom.

c.t: Flanken-cut short ribs 4 to 5 cm thick (sawn across the bones) are best; English-cut short ribs also work.
Choose coconut milk whose only ingredient is "100% coconut milk". Makrut lime leaves are sold in Southeast and South Asian markets, usually frozen.

To turn store-bought red curry paste into panang paste, pound 114 g red curry paste in a mortar with 1 stalk lemongrass (bottom 10–12.5 cm, tender core thinly sliced), 2 tbsp roasted unsalted peanuts, 1/2 whole nutmeg, 2 tsp coriander seeds, 1/2 tsp cumin seeds and 1/2 tsp white peppercorns.
Palm sugar is sold in Thai markets and online. Soften it in the microwave for about 15 seconds, chop and pound it in a mortar, or dissolve it in as little water as possible in a pan.
Najlepšie sú hovädzie rebrá krájané naprieč kosťami (flanken) hrubé 4 až 5 cm; fungujú aj rebrá krájané po jednej kosti (English cut).
Vyberte kokosové mlieko, ktorého jedinou zložkou je „100 % kokosové mlieko“. Listy kafírovej limetky dostanete v juhovýchodoázijských a juhoázijských obchodoch, zvyčajne mrazené.

Palmový cukor dostanete v thajských obchodoch a online. Zmäknete ho asi 15 sekundami v mikrovlnke, nasekaním a roztlčením v mažiari alebo rozpustením v čo najmenšom množstve vody na panvici.

en.t: 1100 g bone-in beef short ribs
3 tbsp (45 ml) vegetable oil, divided
Kosher Salt
240 ml full-fat coconut milk, such as Aroy-D
6 small shallots or pearl onions (about 90 g total), unpeeled
10 fresh or frozen makrut lime leaves, divided
240 ml full-fat coconut milk, such as Aroy-D, divided
114 g homemade or store-bought panang curry paste
3 tbsp (75 g) palm sugar
3 tbsp (45 ml) fish sauce
1 tbsp plus 1 1/2 tsp (30 g) tamarind paste
30 g packed fresh sweet basil leaves (a.k.a. Thai basil)
Cooked jasmine rice, for serving

1. For the Beef Braise: If using flanken-cut ribs, divide each strip into smaller pieces by slicing between the bones; if using English-cut ribs, leave as-is. Season beef all over with salt. In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, heat half of the oil over medium-high heat until lightly smoking. Add half of the beef and cook, turning occasionally, until browned on all sides, about 8 minutes; transfer browned short ribs to a plate. Add remaining oil to pot and repeat browning process with the rest of the beef.

2. Return all beef to the pot, then add enough water to fully cover (about 2000–3000 ml) along with the coconut milk. Bring to a vigorous simmer and cook, stirring occasionally and adding more water as needed to keep beef submerged, until beef is fully tender and can be pierced easily with a paring knife, 2 1/2 to 3 hours. Remove pot from heat and set aside to cool, keeping beef submerged in cooking liquid, for at least 30 minutes. When cool, transfer beef to cutting board. Using a sharp knife, trim off and discard bones and cut beef into 2.5 cm pieces. Set aside, along with 240 ml of beef cooking liquid and 2 tbsp (30 ml) rendered beef fat, which should have risen to surface of cooking liquid; remaining cooking liquid and fat can be refrigerated in an airtight container and saved for another use.

3. Meanwhile, for the Roasted Shallots: Place unpeeled shallots in a small, dry stainless steel or cast iron skillet and cook over medium heat, turning occasionally, until fully softened and blackened all over, about 30 minutes. Alternatively, you can grill the unpeeled shallots over low heat. Transfer shallots to a cutting board, allow to cool until comfortable to handle, then peel. Set aside.

4. For the Curry: Remove and discard the mid-rib from the makrut lime leaves; set half of the leaves aside. Stack remaining makrut lime leaves, fold in half widthwise, then slice into hair-thin strips; set aside separately.

5. In a saucepan, combine reserved 2 tbsp (30 ml) rendered beef fat and 120 ml coconut milk and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook, stirring often with a rubber spatula, until thickened slightly, about 3 minutes.

6. Add curry paste, stir vigorously to combine, and use rubber spatula to scrape the sides of the saucepan to fully incorporate the paste. Add the de-ribbed, whole lime leaves, and continue to cook, stirring and scraping constantly, until the fat begins to separate from the curry paste, about 3 minutes.

7. Add palm sugar and stir to melt. Continue to cook, stirring constantly, until color of paste deepens to a dark brick-red, about 30 seconds. Add fish sauce, tamarind, remaining 120 ml coconut milk, and reserved 240 ml beef cooking liquid, and stir until well incorporated. Add beef and shallots, and gently stir to incorporate into curry. Lower heat to medium-low to maintain a gentle simmer and cook, stirring occasionally and being careful not to break apart the beef, until curry has slightly reduced to a saucy consistency, about 10 minutes. Remove from heat, add sweet basil, and stir until wilted and incorporated.
8. Transfer curry to a large serving bowl or divide between individual bowls and top with remaining thinly-sliced lime leaves. Serve with cooked jasmine rice.

1. Dusené hovädzie: ak máme rebrá krájané naprieč kosťami (flanken), každý pás rozdelíme na menšie kúsky prerezaním medzi kosťami; rebrá krájané pozdĺž kostí (anglický rez) necháme v celku. Mäso zo všetkých strán osolíme. Vo veľkom hrnci s hrubým dnom alebo liatinovom hrnci rozohrejeme na stredne silnom ohni polovicu oleja, kým nezačne jemne dymiť. Vložíme polovicu mäsa a za občasného obracania ho opekáme, kým nie je zo všetkých strán zhnednuté, asi 8 minút; opečené rebrá preložíme na tanier. Do hrnca pridáme zvyšný olej a rovnako opečieme zvyšok mäsa.

2. Všetko mäso vrátime do hrnca, zalejeme toľkou vodou, aby bolo úplne ponorené (asi 2000 – 3000 ml), a pridáme kokosové mlieko. Privedieme do silného varu a za občasného miešania varíme, podľa potreby dolievame vodu, aby mäso zostalo ponorené, kým nie je úplne mäkké a ľahko ho prepichneme nožíkom, 2 ½ až 3 hodiny. Hrniec odstavíme a necháme chladnúť aspoň 30 minút; mäso pritom necháme ponorené vo výpare. Vychladnuté mäso preložíme na dosku. Ostrým nožom odrežeme a vyhodíme kosti a mäso nakrájame na 2,5 cm kúsky. Odložíme spolu s 240 ml výparu a 2 PL (30 ml) vyškvareného hovädzieho tuku, ktorý by mal vyplávať na povrch; zvyšný výpar a tuk môžeme vo vzduchotesnej nádobe uložiť do chladničky a použiť inokedy.

3. Medzitým opečené šalotky: neolúpané šalotky dáme do malej suchej panvice z nehrdzavejúcej ocele alebo liatiny a na strednom ohni ich za občasného obracania opekáme, kým úplne nezmäknú a nie sú celé sčernené, asi 30 minút. Prípadne ich môžeme ugrilovať neolúpané na miernom ohni. Šalotky preložíme na dosku, necháme vychladnúť, kým sa ich dá pohodlne dotknúť, a olúpeme. Odložíme.

4. Kari: z listov kafírovej limetky odstránime a vyhodíme strednú žilku; polovicu listov odložíme. Zvyšné listy položíme na seba, priečne preložíme na polovicu a nakrájame na tenučké prúžky; odložíme zvlášť.

5. V hrnci zmiešame odložené 2 PL (30 ml) vyškvareného hovädzieho tuku a 120 ml kokosového mlieka a na strednom ohni privedieme do mierneho varu. Za častého miešania gumenou stierkou varíme, kým trochu nezhustne, asi 3 minúty.

6. Pridáme kari pastu, energicky premiešame a gumenou stierkou zoškrabujeme steny hrnca, aby sa pasta úplne zapracovala. Pridáme celé listy kafírovej limetky bez žiliek a za stáleho miešania a zoškrabovania varíme, kým sa tuk od pasty nezačne oddeľovať, asi 3 minúty.

7. Pridáme palmový cukor a miešame, kým sa neroztopí. Za stáleho miešania varíme ďalej, kým pasta nestmavne do tmavej tehlovočervenej farby, asi 30 sekúnd. Pridáme rybaciu omáčku, tamarind, zvyšných 120 ml kokosového mlieka a odložených 240 ml výparu a miešame, kým sa dobre nespoja. Pridáme mäso a šalotky a jemne ich vmiešame do kari. Oheň stiahneme na stredne slabý, aby sa kari len mierne varilo, a za občasného miešania varíme, pričom dávame pozor, aby sa mäso nerozpadlo, kým sa kari mierne nezredukuje na omáčku, asi 10 minút. Odstavíme, pridáme sladkú bazalku a miešame, kým nezvädne a nezapracuje sa.
8. Kari preložíme do veľkej servírovacej misy alebo rozdelíme do misiek a posypeme zvyšnými prúžkami listov kafírovej limetky. Podávame s uvarenou jazmínovou ryžou.

c.t: Use the right paste: look for "karee" or "kari" besides "yellow", not "yellow sour curry". A picture with potato chunks on the label is a good sign.
Použite správnu pastu: hľadajte okrem slova „yellow“ aj „karee“ alebo „kari“, nie „yellow sour curry“. Dobrým znamením je obrázok s kúskami zemiakov na obale.

en.t: 1/2 English cucumber
2 large shallots or 1/2 medium red onion, peeled and sliced thinly lengthwise
1 green or red jalapeno pepper, sliced thinly crosswise
99 g granulated sugar
120 ml white distilled vinegar (no substitute)
2 tbsp (30 ml) water
1/2 tsp (3 g) salt
59 ml kari (karee) curry paste
355 ml full-fat coconut milk
455 g low-starch, waxy potatoes, peeled (optional) and cut into 5 cm cubes
455 g medium yellow or white onions, peeled and cut lengthwise into 6 wedges
2 tbsp (30 ml) fish sauce, or to taste
455 g boneless, skinless chicken breasts or thighs, cut into 5 cm cubes

1. Cut the half cucumber in half lengthwise. With the cut side down, cut each half crosswise into thin slices; place in a glass bowl. Add shallot (or red onion) slices and pepper slices to cucumber bowl; set aside.

2. Combine sugar, vinegar, water, and salt in a small saucepan. Set over medium heat and cook, stirring occasionally until sugar has completely dissolved (the mixture doesn't have to be boiled), immediately remove from heat. Allow the sauce to cool down to slightly warmer than room temperature, then pour it over cucumber-shallot-pepper mixture. Stir, cover with a piece of plastic wrap, and keep chilled.

3. In a 1890 ml saucepan set over medium-high heat, heat about 120 ml of coconut cream (the thick part that rises to the top of the can) with curry paste. c.t: 1. Cut the half cucumber in half lengthwise. With the cut side down, cut each half crosswise into thin slices; place in a glass bowl. Add shallot (or red onion) slices and pepper slices to cucumber bowl; set aside.

2. Combine sugar, vinegar, water, and salt in a small saucepan. Set over medium heat and cook, stirring occasionally until sugar has completely dissolved (the mixture doesn't have to be boiled), immediately remove from heat. Allow the sauce to cool down to slightly warmer than room temperature, then pour it over cucumber-shallot-pepper mixture. Stir, cover with a piece of plastic wrap, and keep chilled.

3. In a 1890 ml saucepan set over medium-high heat, heat about 120 ml of coconut cream (the thick part that rises to the top of the can) with curry paste. Once coconut fat splits, add potato, onion, remaining coconut milk, and fish sauce to the saucepan. Add just enough water, if necessary, to keep the ingredients submerged. Bring to a boil; cover, lower the heat so the mixture simmers, and cook, stirring occasionally, until potatoes cubes are softened, about 15 minutes.

2. V malom hrnci zmiešame cukor, ocot, vodu a soľ. Postavíme na stredný oheň a za občasného miešania zohrievame, kým sa cukor úplne nerozpustí (zmes netreba privádzať do varu), a hneď odstavíme. Nálev necháme vychladnúť, kým nie je len o niečo teplejší ako izbová teplota, potom ním zalejeme zmes uhorky, šalotky a papričky. Premiešame, prikryjeme potravinovou fóliou a necháme vychladiť.

3. V 1890 ml hrnci na stredne silnom ohni zohrejeme asi 120 ml kokosovej smotany (hustej časti, ktorá vystúpi navrch plechovky) s kari pastou. Keď sa kokosový tuk oddelí, pridáme do hrnca zemiaky, cibuľu, zvyšné kokosové mlieko a rybaciu omáčku. Ak treba, prilejeme len toľko vody, aby boli suroviny ponorené. Privedieme do varu, prikryjeme, oheň stiahneme, aby sa zmes mierne varila, a za občasného miešania varíme, kým kocky zemiakov nezmäknú, asi 15 minút.
4. Do hrnca pridáme kuracie mäso. Zmes opäť privedieme do mierneho varu, prikryjeme a varíme, kým mäso nie je hotové, 5 až 8 minút. Ochutnáme a podľa potreby pridáme ďalšiu rybaciu omáčku.

en.t: 1 tsp (4 g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt
20 dried Thai chiles (8 g), stemmed
15 fresh green or red Thai chiles (15 g), stemmed

4 medium garlic cloves (20 g)
2 small shallots (40 g), quartered
1 tbsp (30 g) Thai shrimp paste
3 tbsp (80 g) tamarind paste
1 1/2 tsp (12 g) palm sugar
3 tbsp (45 ml) fish sauce
185 g green papaya, peeled and cut into 5 cm by 1.5 cm-thick pieces, from 1 green papaya
Two (170 g) skin-on red snapper fillets, cut into 5 cm pieces

1. For the Curry Paste: If Using a Mortar and Pestle: Combine salt and dried chiles in a granite mortar and pestle and pound until chiles are broken down into small pieces, about 2 minutes. Pounding thoroughly between each addition to break down and incorporate ingredients into the paste (3 to 4 minutes of pounding per addition), add in the following order: fresh chiles; turmeric; garlic and shallots; shrimp paste. It should take about 15 minutes total to pound ingredients into a very fine paste with just a few visible pieces of fresh chile skin. If Using a Blender: Combine salt, dried and fresh chiles, turmeric, garlic, shallots, and shrimp paste in a blender jar with 240 ml water. Blend on high speed until smooth, 2 to 3 minutes.

2. For the Curry, If Using Pounded Paste: In a saucepan, whisk together curry paste and 240 ml water until well combined. Once thoroughly incorporated, add 710 ml water, tamarind, palm sugar, and fish sauce, and stir to combine. If Using Blended Paste: In a saucepan, combine curry paste, 710 ml water, tamarind, palm sugar, and fish sauce and stir to combine.

3. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, add papaya and cook, stirring occasionally, until papaya is just beginning to soften but is still crunchy, 5 to 7 minutes. You may notice foam rising to the surface; this is normal, and should not be skimmed.

4. Add snapper and, using a spoon, gently submerge pieces in the curry. Continue to cook, gently stirring occasionally, until fish is opaque and just cooked through, 2 to 3 minutes. Remove from heat, and stir in lime juice.
5. Transfer curry to a large serving bowl or divide between individual bowls. Serve immediately with cooked jasmine rice.
